candidates.source_title: This £2.50 bus ride is the best thing to cross the Pennines since Eric Cantona
candidates.source_summary: From the top deck of the 590 you can take a trip through Greater Manchester's rich industrial heritage while taking in some of the the region's most dramatic scenery
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Eric Cantona, the M62 and the Industrial Revolution. Despite the long animosity between Lancashire and Yorkshire a few things have successfully made the journey across the Pennines. And to that list you can add the 590 bus . The Rochdale to Halifax service swaps the Roch Valley for the Calder Valley as it crosses over from Greater Manchester into West Yorkshire. And along the way it takes in two marvels of the Industrial Revolution and plenty of the region's most dramatic scenery. I caught the 590 this week as far as Hebden Bridge as part of our occasional series on Greater Manchester's most scenic bus routes . Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The first thing to note is because this is a privately-owned First Bus and not a publicly-controlled Bee Network service a single ticket is £2.50 not two quid. Having stumped up the extra 10 bob, I head upstairs to join a handful of students heading home after lectures on the top deck. From Rochdale bus station it heads east out of the town centre through Smallbridge and Littleborough before crossing the border at Summit into the towns of Walsden, Todmorden and Hebden Bridge. It's a pretty unremarkable start to the journey, but soon the chicken shops and rows of brick terraces start to give way to old weavers cottages and Rochdale's famous flagstone fences. Up ahead the dramatic gritstone ridge of Blackstone Edge, marking the border between Greater Manchester and West Yorkshire, looms on the horizon. At Littleborough the bus turns north and as we begin the head into the hills we pass the former studio of the late Walter Kershaw. The painter was dubbed the 'Original Banksy' for his huge street murals and through the dusty bay window a number of his canvases can be seen still hung on the wall. At the crest of the hill, at the aptly-named village of Summit, we pass the mouth of the Summit Tunnel, a George Stephenson-designed miracle of Victorian engineering. When it opened in 1841, providing a direct link between the industrial powerhouses of Manchester and Leeds, it was the longest railway tunnel in the world. In 1984 it was also the scene of one of the biggest underground fires in transport history when a train carrying a million litres of petrol derailed. As temperatures inside reached a staggering 1,500C it took firefighters four days to extinguish the blaze. And it’s not the only reminder of our ancestors’ ingenuity along the route. To the right the Rochdale Canal, which opened 37 years before the tunnel, follows the same path along the valley. Don't let an algorithm decide what Manchester news you see - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Painstakingly dug by hand, at 600ft above sea level it’s one of the highest canals in England. In years gone by hundreds of barges would have transported cotton, wool, coal and timber between Lancashire and Yorkshire. Today you’re much more likely to see a few pleasure cruisers eking out the last of the summer or, as I did near Walsden, a group of kayakers going for a paddle. As we approach the border with Yorkshire we also get a glimpse of a herd of alpacas, a long way from their native South America, grazing in a field of the far bank of the canal. Developer and investment manager Chancerygate is delivering Birch 100 at Birch Business Park in Heywood, with Barnfield Construction appointed as main contractor. Practical completion is expected in summer 2027, with the development targeting BREEAM Excellent and an EPC A rating. It will also feature solar photovoltaic panels and electric vehicle charging. Chancerygate acquired the 410,000sq ft, 32-acre business park in July 2025 and has since completed refurbishment work on three units ranging from 11,720sq ft to 30,590sq ft. Located close to the M66 and M62, the estate’s occupiers include Vodafone, Restore, JOST and Archbold Logistics. Birch Business Park also sits within the 1600-acre Northern Gateway employment allocation, which is expected to deliver up to 11.5 million sq ft of new employment space across the Bury and Rochdale border.

candidates.source_title: Residents’ fears over fast-food restaurant’s 3am plans - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Residents have raised concerns about a fast-food restaurant's late-licence plan.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Residents have raised concerns about a fast-food restaurant’s late-licence plan. Rochdale Council has received an application for the Burger Box, at the former Haibat Sultan restaurant at 26 Milkstone Road, to stay open until 3am daily. The council’s Licensing Sub-Committee will meet on Monday, October 12, to determine the application which names Kashif Hazarbuz as the premises licence holder. The Burger Box is described as a fast-food restaurant in a ground-floor retail unit with residential accommodation above, situated on a busy main road. Planning permission has been granted for eat-in, collection and delivery service from 11am to 11pm Monday to Sunday, and 11am to 10pm on Sundays and bank holidays. The licensing application looks to extend this to 3am each day. Under the terms of the premises licence, no alcohol can be taken into or be consumed in the restaurant at any time. Among the objections, Mrs S Rana believes that that there will be an increase in anti-social behaviour and noise from the restaurant. She is also concerned that there will be an increase in traffic and pollution if the licence is granted until 3am. candidates.source_summary: A notorious former asbestos factory known as 'Rochdale's Chernobyl' is a step closer to redevelopment after landowners appointed a specialist clean-up contractor.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: 'Rochdale's Chernobyl' is a step closer to redevelopment after landowners appointed a specialist contractor to clean up the notorious former asbestos factory site. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale. It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long-held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Many locals would like to see the site transformed into a park that blends with the surrounding greenery. But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement is the appointment of a specialist contractor to carry out remediation work on the site. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Saturday saw Saints make the trip to Rochdale Rugby Club, perched on the edge of the Pennines, for their second game of the season. A fine, bright, warm day and a good pitch greeted the visitors. Injuries continue to affect Saints early in the campaign, with another three regular starters unavailable, although it was a welcome boost to see Oscar Crow and Niall Grant return on the bench. Saints made the early running, but Rochdale’s determined scrambling defence held firm until winger Sam Cotgrave barged his way over in the corner. Smith added the conversion while on kicking duties for the day. Rochdale then began to grow into the game, and with Smith shown a yellow card, the hosts took advantage. A well-worked try following missed tackles in the centre was converted to level the scores at 7-7. Rochdale missed several further scoring opportunities through dropped balls and a forward pass before eventually finding space to score beneath the posts, with the conversion giving them a 14-7 lead in front of a vocal home crowd. Saints responded well. After a penalty was kicked to touch six metres out, the resulting drive towards the line saw Joe Sanders cross for a try, with Ben Jones converting to make it 14-14. Saints continued to apply pressure, but Rochdale resisted until Olly Dodd sidestepped his defender and crossed on the stroke of half-time. Smith added the conversion on his return from the sin bin to give Saints a 21-14 lead at the break. Saints started the second half strongly, but a forced pass was spilled and Rochdale pounced, racing over in the corner. The conversion was missed, reducing the deficit to 21-19. The visitors quickly regained control. Changes in personnel helped Saints gain the upper hand in the scrum, which was beginning to take its toll on the Rochdale pack. After another attack close to the line, prop John Whittaker was driven over for a converted try, extending the lead to 28-19 and securing a bonus point. Saints were beginning to dominate possession, although Rochdale’s defence remained stubborn. A powerful scrum drive 10 metres out allowed Kincart to find Cotgrave, who slipped around his defender to score his second try of the afternoon. The conversion made it 35-19. Rochdale continued to throw everything into the contest. They were held up over the line before taking a quick tap penalty from an earlier offside offence, catching the Saints defence napping to score. The conversion was missed, but the hosts earned a deserved bonus point as the score moved to 35-24. Saints had the final say. Captain Will Grebe powered towards the line and, despite being tackled, somehow stretched out to ground the ball and score. The conversion was missed, but it completed a 40-24 victory for the visitors. It was not Saints’ best performance and they have yet to field a full-strength squad this season, but an away win and five league points represented a productive afternoon. Next up is a trip to Vale of Lune, with a 3pm kick-off. candidates.source_body_excerpt: SATURDAY saw Saints make the trip to Rochdale Rugby Club perched on the edge of the Pennines. A fine bright warm day and good pitch greeted the visitors for the second game of the season with injuries again blighting the squad with three regular starters missing but the return of Oscar Crow and Niall Grant on the bench. From the start it was Saints going forward but the solid, scrambling defence of Rochdale held firm until winger Sam Cotgrave barged his way into the corner, converted by Billy Smith who was on kicking duties. Rochdale then really started to find their way into the game with Saints player Smith yellow carded, firstly with a well worked try after missed tackles in the centre converted to make the score 7-7. Rochdale wasted three more try scoring opportunities with a couple of dropped balls and a forward pass, until finally finding space to score under the posts converted for a 14-7 lead in front of a vocal home crowd. Saints pressed again and a penalty to touch six metres out was driven towards the line where Joe Sanders went over with Ben Jones converting to bring it back to 14-14. Again Saints piled on the pressure but Rochdale held firm until Olly Dodd sidestepped the defender before going over the whitewash on the stroke of halftime converted by Smith on his yellow card return. It was Saints who came out straight into attack but a forced pass was spilled and pounced on by Rochdale who raced over in the corner to pull it back to 19-21 as the conversion was missed.

candidates.source_summary: Middleton could have two adult gaming arcades within feet of each other if new plans get the green light.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Middleton could have two adult gaming arcades within feet of each other if new plans get the green light. JR Planning Consultants has applied to Rochdale Council to turn the Subway store at 16 Middleton Gardens into an adult gaming centre. It follows an application it submitted in July to turn the premises into a nail bar. That application has since been withdrawn. In the latest application, JR Planning said the Planning Inspectorate appeal which allowed Jeffries Casino to occupy the former Virgin Money premises at 20 Middleton Gardens had set a precedent for the change of use in a retail area. It said: “The Inspector found that the proposed adult gaming centre was likely to generate greater footfall over a typical day than many potential Class E uses. “The Inspector also found that the use would provide opportunities for linked trips to shops, pubs and other town centre businesses and make a modest contribution to the functioning of the centre. “It was concluded that the adult gaming centre would form part of a suitable mix of uses complementary to the retail role of Middleton town centre. Therefore, the vitality and viability of the centre would not be undermined. “The Inspector also considered the potential concentration of adult gaming centres. It was concluded that the establishment of an additional non-retail unit would not be materially harmful to the vitality and viability of the town centre.

candidates.source_summary: Swindon Town are bracing themselves for fitness reports on three more players following their 1-0 defeat at Rochdale
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Swindon Town are bracing themselves for fitness reports on three more players following their 1-0 defeat at Rochdale . Ian Holloway’s squad was down to the bare bones at the Crown Oil Arena, as Cian Hayes’ late header denied them a first away point since the opening day of the season . Swindon switched formation for the game to make a team around the available players, and there was not much help on the bench, with only James Debayo fully fit, and this was shown in the use of substitutions , as Town did not make a tactical switch until second-half stoppage time. Ollie Clarke was not initially meant to be in the squad, but he powered through a niggle and came on for Tom Nichols, who had gone down with a knock with around 25 minutes to play. Joseph Hungbo also had to be convinced to travel with the squad, as he was dealing with discomfort in his knee, but Holloway explained to him that he couldn’t lose anyone else, and so he played the final six minutes. But the possible casualties could have serious consequences for Swindon, as, along with Nichols, Aaron Drinan went down off the ball and was stretching out his hamstring before eventually being replaced, and Jack Thomson was also struggling with a cramp before he was replaced. Thomson and Drinan have been two of the players Town have relied on during this period, as both have played 90 minutes consistently. Who showed promise and who won the real duel? candidates.source_summary: After decades of decay, Rochdale's Chernobyl is finally getting cleaned up Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale . It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Creating a park, to seamlessly blend with the surrounding greenery, is the popular option for locals. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement has been to sign a contractor to deliver the clean up of the site - remediation. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development When the Manchester Evening News toured the site last year , the foliage at head height was hard to ignore, as was the level of deterioration of the old factory buildings themselves. It is unknown what the remediation work will actually entail, but some level of demolition work could be included as part of it. candidates.source_title: New governor will help ease pressure on gas network - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: New equipment could be installed to help meet demand for gas in an area of Middleton.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: New equipment could be installed to help meet demand for gas in an area of Middleton. MacMarshalls Rural Chartered Surveyors & Planning Consultants has applied on behalf of Cadent Gas Ltd to Rochdale Council to install a new gas governor, kiosk and fencing next to 56 Bonscale Crescent in Middleton. The kiosk is earmarked for a corner of the open space — which also includes a children’s play area — closest to the road and against the boundary with 56 Bonscale Crescent. The application follows a previous plan to install the kiosk beside 54 Bonscale Crescent. That application was withdrawn. In planning documents submitted to the council, MacMarshalls said: “The works are driven by current pressure on the existing gas network, which means a new gas governor is required to cope with demand for gas in the local area. “Gas governors are essential to the safe distribution of gas and are designed to control gas pressure in the locality, reducing pressure from high to low in order to feed local residents and businesses. “Gas usage in the area is high from both commercial and residential end users, and the local area is therefore reliant on the gas governor, hence the requirement to install a new kiosk in this area. “The kiosk itself would not, as a standalone operation, require planning permission, as it would fall within the permitted parameters. The proposed kiosk is 26.8 cubic metres, with permitted development allowing for the installation of a structure for housing apparatus not exceeding 29 cubic metres.

The under-fire Robins boss, who described himself as a “dead man walking” during a viral interview in the build-up to the game, felt his patched-up side deserved a share of the spoils. But Cian Hayes headed the winning goal in the 88th minute for Rochdale, three minutes after the dismissal of Kaelan Majekodunmi for a second bookable offence. “I thought it was a fantastic performance from the lads and the game turned on a couple of moments,” said Holloway. “Were the bookings really bookings? And then the ball has hit someone in the face and they score. It’s just the way it’s gone for us. “We had two good chances in the second half and we had to take one of them. Had we done that, it’s a different game. “The lads worked their socks off and it’s fine margins. One of our lads gets smashed in the head. He’s having treatment and they go and score! “It’s an absolutely rubbish rule, not everybody is cheating and lying down waiting for treatment. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Swindon boss Ian Holloway praised his injury-hit squad’s performance despite a 1-0 defeat at Rochdale. The under-fire Robins boss, who described himself as a “dead man walking” during a viral interview in the build-up to the game, felt his patched-up side deserved a share of the spoils. But Cian Hayes headed the winning goal in the 88th minute for Rochdale, three minutes after the dismissal of Kaelan Majekodunmi for a second bookable offence. “I thought it was a fantastic performance from the lads and the game turned on a couple of moments,” said Holloway. “Were the bookings really bookings? And then the ball has hit someone in the face and they score. It’s just the way it’s gone for us. “We had two good chances in the second half and we had to take one of them. Had we done that, it’s a different game. “The lads worked their socks off and it’s fine margins. One of our lads gets smashed in the head. Cian Hayes headed a late winner as Rochdale capitalised on Swindon having a man sent off to secure a 1-0 victory and increase the pressure on Ian Holloway.

Under-fire Robins' boss Holloway branded himself a "dead man walking" in a viral pre-match interview but his side looked to have done enough to secure a welcome point at the Crown Oil Arena.

But Kaelan Majekodunmi was sent off for a second bookable offence in the 85th minute and Rochdale struck three minutes later to snatch the points as Hayes glanced home Aden Flint's knock-on.

Neither goalkeeper had been seriously tested in the opening half, though it took Flint's timely intervention to prevent Anthony Munda's low drive from troubling Nils Ramming in the Rochdale goal.

After the interval, Antwoine Hackford was denied by Ramming while Rochdale frontman Dajaune Brown missed a golden opportunity in the 66th minute when he got his feet in a tangle and failed to convert Glenn Middleton's inviting delivery.

Brown saw a volleyed effort pushed over the bar by Connor Ripley, who later saved brilliantly from Charlie Tasker before Hayes delivered the decisive blow.

But Cian Hayes headed the winning goal in the 88th minute for Rochdale, three minutes after the dismissal of Kaelan Majekodunmi for a second bookable offence. “I thought it was a fantastic performance from the lads and the game turned on a couple of moments,” said Holloway. “Were the bookings really bookings? And then the ball has hit someone in the face and they score. It’s just the way it’s gone for us. “We had two good chances in the second half and we had to take one of them. Had we done that, it’s a different game. “The lads worked their socks off and it’s fine margins. One of our lads gets smashed in the head. He’s having treatment and they go and score! “It’s an absolutely rubbish rule, not everybody is cheating and lying down waiting for treatment. Why don’t they use their common sense and change the rules? My centre half is off the field receiving treatment and it should be their bloke, the one who clobbered him, who should be off the field.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Cian Hayes headed a late winner as Rochdale capitalised on Swindon having a man sent off to secure a 1-0 victory and increase the pressure on Ian Holloway. Under-fire Robins’ boss Holloway branded himself a “dead man walking” in a viral pre-match interview but his side looked to have done enough to secure a welcome point at the Crown Oil Arena. But Kaelan Majekodunmi was sent off for a second bookable offence in the 85th minute and Rochdale struck three minutes later to snatch the points as Hayes glanced home Aden Flint’s knock-on. Neither goalkeeper had been seriously tested in the opening half, though it took Flint’s timely intervention to prevent Anthony Munda’s low drive from troubling Nils Ramming in the Rochdale goal. After the interval, Antwoine Hackford was denied by Ramming while Rochdale frontman Dajaune Brown missed a golden opportunity in the 66th minute when he got his feet in a tangle and failed to convert Glenn Middleton’s inviting delivery. Brown saw a volleyed effort pushed over the bar by Connor Ripley, who later saved brilliantly from Charlie Tasker before Hayes delivered the decisive blow.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: It was heartbreak for ten-man Swindon Town as a last-minute goal saw them defeated 1-0 on the road at Rochdale. The first half was lacking in attacking quality from both sides, and Swindon will have been pleased with their ability to frustrate their hosts. Swindon started the second half very well, but a late red card for Kaelan Majekodunmi proved a bridge too far, and Cian Hayes headed home the winner. Amidst all the struggles it was a strong effort, but they are without a goal in 630 minutes of football away from home, and have taken just one point. Faced with a major injury crisis, Ian Holloway made three changes to his starting 11. Late calls were made to have Ollie Clarke and Joseph Hungbo on the bench, but they dropped out, along with Paul Glatzel, for Tom Nichols, Billy Kirkman, and Antwoine Hackford. With all the changes, Swindon went with a slightly different 4-4-2 system to try to get the most out of the available players. The ethos to have a disciplined shape that can be pressed from remained This brought an early opportunity, as Anthony Munda rushed Harvey Gilmour, allowing Tom Nichols to pounce on a loose pass. Antwoine Hackford was eventually fouled on the edge of the box, but James Ball’s free kick was tame. Swindon were clogging up the middle, but there was space for Glenn Middleton on the Rochdale left. The winger was able to run at Ball a few times early on and put crosses into the box.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week's faith news from the Rochdale area Last Sunday we had our joint Harvest Festival at St Barnabas Church taken by Revd Roger Hill and this week we will celebrate Holy Communion officiated by Revd Ian Stamp. The service will be followed by tea, coffee and biscuits giving us all a time to chat and get to know each other and also any visitors who are usually among us. We will meet again this Tuesday for prayer and Bible study at a member's house looking at the Gospel of Luke and finding out what the Lord has to say to us through this. As we have said before in Faith News, we have sadly reached the decision to disband our Holy Trinity Youth Theatre Workshop. We used to perform two productions each year which were very successful and have now found that we need some space so have been selling most of the costumes since we have ended the theatre group. The reason, as we have said here before, is due to the fact that the costs of producing shows have for us become rather excessive. That being said, we feel sad for the children who thoroughly enjoyed being connected with the production and the confidence that they found. Due to this decision, we still have many boxes of unsold costumes. We have been exceptionally lucky because when we decided to dispose of some costumes we found that societies throughout the world were interested in buying some. There are also some backcloths available too. We have sold some to societies in Germany, Italy, Norway and America, not bad for a little church in Littleborough. Indeed, our first Joseph and first Wizard of Oz costumes were sold to professional theatre companies in England. But our The King and I costumes have been to an American company. That having been said, we have successfully sold some on eBay. However, we still have lots of costumes to sell including some military items. Ironically, we still have some of the nun costumes from The Sound of Music, so if you are interested please contact Holy Trinity Littleborough.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: An exhibition about the Warsaw Uprising of 1944 was launched at the Fusilier Museum in Bury on Thursday evening, October 1. Warsaw Calling: Uprising 1944 explores the Polish underground resistance’s uprising against Nazi occupation, which began on August 1, 1944. Resistance fighters and civilians fought for the liberation of Warsaw for 63 days. The exhibition uses personal stories, archival material and images to tell the stories of those who lived through the uprising. It was curated by the Polish Underground Movement Study Trust in partnership with Polonia Northern England. A complementary display, Northern Heroines, tells the stories of three women connected to the Polish community in the North of England. It was produced by Polonia Northern England. Warsaw Calling: Uprising 1944 runs until February 27, 2027. Entry is included in museum admission. The museum is on Moss Street, Bury, BL9 0DF. Admission costs £4.95 for adults, £3.95 for concessions, £2.95 for children and £9.95 for families. Tickets include an annual pass allowing repeat visits for 12 months.

candidates.source_title: Details of new Scout Moor wind farm revealed
candidates.source_summary: A new wind farm planned for moorland between Rochdale and Bury has reduced in size, but it’s still not good enough for opposing campaigners.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A new wind farm planned for moorland between Rochdale and Bury has reduced in size, but it’s still not good enough for opposing campaigners. The Say NO to Scout Moor 2 group has objected to Cubico Sustainable Investments plan for ‘Scout Moor 2’ ever since they were first mooted back in 2024. Campaigners fear the turbines – up to 180m including blade tip height – would be larger than Blackpool Tower and dominate the skyline. The latest changes from Cubico have seen the scheme dropped from 17 wind turbines to 12. This reduction means that the proposed windfarm would only have the potential to power 84,552 homes annually, rather than 100,000 previously touted. There is already a wind farm in operation on Scout Moor. But according to planning documents, the farm would be run separately and have a life span of around 40 years. Planning papers also highlight the need for underground cables connected to an on-site substation, which will later be hooked up to a supply point in Rossendale to deliver electricity to the National Grid. The clean energy generation from the turbines is said to recover the fossil fuel costs to build the new wind farm in 18 months. They’ve also said the excavation of peat, a pivotal carbon dioxide capture source, will be reduced by 28 per cent. Cubico has promised a peat restoration project so the extracted peat will not be lost entirely. This is something objectors don’t believe is realistic. Cubico also said they are avoiding placing turbines that dominate local viewpoints. But these statements have also been challenged by local campaigners.

candidates.source_title: Could the Turner Brothers factory finally be getting cleared up
candidates.source_summary: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale. It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Creating a park, to seamlessly blend with the surrounding greenery, is the popular option for locals. But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement has been to sign a contractor to deliver the clean up of the site – remediation. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development

Sondheim’s glorious songs, including the bittersweet ‘Send in the Clowns’, bring wit and romance to this Tony Award-winning musical comedy.
